Hello, to start off, I do browse the KiA sub on Reddit, but I'm more of a lurker since I've had suspicions that I'll get shadowbanned for not thinking that a smug group of ne'er-do-wells isn't exactly qualified for being moral guardians.

To start off, I found out about GamerGate (or rather the beginnings of it) browsing TumblrInAction. I had been critical of the Tumblr SJW crowd ever since one of my friends started talking about their nonsense (he's since left Tumblr to focus on college). Normally, I treated them as just kind of a small, loudmouthed group of teens that were giving ill-founded opinions about the world around them, but I soon learned the treat they actually posed during the mass censorship of various websites. So, I felt it was in my best interest to make sure a longtime hobby of mine wasn't being taken over by ideological crazies.

I suppose in terms of fairness, I'm not entirely sure GamerGate is in the complete "right", but it stands for many things I care deeply about, such as Free Speech, being judged for actions rather than someone's race or gender, and trust. In fact, I'd say more than anything GamerGate is about trust. A trust that was broken by censor-happy moderators and nepotistic journalists. Plus, the Anti-GG faction has to be one of the most vitriolic and mean-spirited collective I've ever laid witness too. I really don't like them. Only think they're good for is coming up with funny names for GamerGate (Gobbledygook is probably my favorite).

It's also started to affect me personally, as a few of my friends have fallen to the dark side. Thankfully, most of my friends and family are either Pro-GG or at least neutral / don't care, although most of the Pro ones are afraid of speaking out for fear of being branded a woman-hater, despite many of them being gay. One friend in particular has been grumbling on Tumblr lately reblogging anti-gamer nonsense (despite him being a pretty avid one himself...I don't understand this kind of thinking at all.) There's also been a few people I (used to) look up to buy into these horrible lies as well, and showing a great deal of hypocrisy as a result. It's very disheartening to see this bizarro logic overtake things you care about.

However, I am very relieved to see people fight against a mainstream media campaign of lies, hostile journalists trying to get their readerbase back (maybe it wasn't such a good idea to slander a group of people you write for), and even some internal drama. Keep up the good work, everyone.
